newsitem.title: USA: US congressman minimizes Boeing concessions to EU.
newsitem.headline: US congressman minimizes Boeing concessions to EU.

text.p: United States congressman Jack Metcalf said Wednesday a key concession Boeing made to win the European Union's blessing of its merger with McDonnell Douglas was merely face-saving.

Boeing agreed not to enforce controversial 20-year exclusivity provisions in its existing supply agremeents with AMR's American Airlines, Delta Air Lines and Continental Airlines Inc., and not to make any other such agreements for 10 years.

"Congressional and executive pressure (on the EU) prevented Boeing from giving up any firm orders as the Europeans had demanded," said the Republican from Washington state, who has a major Boeing plant in his district. "Giving up the exclusive contracts in name only is more face saving for Europe than any great concession."
Metcalf was one of several Washington State elected officials who took the lead in fighting for Boeing in Congress.

Late on Tuesday, the House of Representatives approved a "sense of the House" resolution by Metcalf, with a vote of 416 to 2. It stated that EU disapproval would constitute "unwarranted and unprecedented interference" in an American business transaction.
